inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL training exercise calculates TIMESTAMPDIFF in minutes, aggregates durations, finds minimum and maximum values, and investigates negative-duration data-quality anomalies.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored grouped exam-session duration audit. Fixed start and end timestamps exercise minute differences, negative and zero durations, NULL endpoints, COUNT of measured sessions, AVG/MIN/MAX, anomaly counts, CASE classification, and deterministic group ordering; the source tables, rows, labels, and answers are not copied.

fixture_notes: Rows cover positive, negative, zero, and NULL durations across three exam groups so minute arithmetic and data-quality classification remain observable.
determinism_notes: All session IDs and timestamps are fixed literals, and output is ordered by the grouped exam name with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE exam_sessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, exam_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, start_at DATETIME NULL, end_at DATETIME NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT exam_name, COUNT(*) AS session_count, COUNT(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) AS measured_count, AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) AS average_minutes, MIN(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) AS shortest_minutes, MAX(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) AS longest_minutes, SUM(CASE WHEN TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at) < 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS negative_count, CASE WHEN MIN(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) IS NULL THEN 'unmeasured' WHEN MIN(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, start_at, end_at)) < 0 THEN 'has-anomaly' ELSE 'valid' END AS duration_class FROM exam_sessions GROUP BY exam_name ORDER BY exam_name
